name: Gahar
overview: Gahar is a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant highlights his participation in the religious duties associated with the Levitical tribe. Beyond this, no additional personal details or notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Gahar means "[born in the] year of little rain," which may reflect the circumstances of his birth or a particular time of significance. This proper name is not indicated as being given by God, and it is recorded in Ezra 2:47.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Gahar as a descendant of Levi, connecting him to the Levitical lineage responsible for temple service. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Gahar's significance lies in his role as a temple servant within the tribe of Levi, emphasizing the continuity of Levitical duties during the post-exilic period. His mention in Ezra 2:47 situates him among those who returned to Jerusalem and participated in restoring temple worship. This underscores the faithfulness of God's people in preserving their sacred responsibilities after exile.
